newsitem.title: GHANA: Historic election win for Ghana's Rawlings.
newsitem.headline: Historic election win for Ghana's Rawlings.

text.p: President Jerry Rawlings, who has dominated national life in Ghana for almost two decades, won a historic election victory on Wednesday becoming its first incumbent to be re-elected since independence in 1957.

National Election Commission chairman Kwadwo Afari-Gyan told a news conference Rawlings had won a final four-year term with 57.2 percent of votes cast against 39.9 percent for his main rival John Kufuor of the opposition's Great Alliance.

Jubilant supporters of Rawlings, who has twice seized power in the West African nation and is still only 49, took to the streets of central Accra, the capital, singing and dancing and sounding vehicle horns. They carried flags and banners.
Kufuor, 58, a seasoned politician and businessman who led the opposition challenge in Saturday's presidential and parliamentary elections, congratulated Rawlings on his win.
"I congratulate him for being declared the winner," he said in a live telephone interview on state radio, adding that he hoped Rawlings would become a less partisan leader.
"I wish him well, in the national interest I wish reconciliation will be a hall-mark of his regime, I wish he will be a bit more open, especially to the opposition," he added.
Rawlings said on Tuesday that Ghana's political family needed to work together to build the nation.
"We are members of one family. We will not be vindictive. There is much work ahead and we need to work together to build the country," he said when meeting a group of poll monitors.
The turnout in Saturday's elections was 76.8 percent.
In the contest for parliament's 200 seats Rawlings's National Democratic Congress won 130 seats and the combined opposition a total of 65.
Afari-Gyan said the presidential results were based on 197 of the West African nation's 200 constituencies. Results of five seats in the parliamentary poll had yet to be announced.

Commonwealth and Organisation of African Unity observers have paid tribute to the conduct and fairness of the elections. "This is by far the best organised election I have seen in West Africa," one Western monitor said.
Despite tension and some violence in the run-up to voting, polling day itself passed off smoothly. Some observers spoke of a few lapses in the organisation of the poll.
Since independence from Britain, all Ghana's elected governments -- except that of Rawlings -- have been toppled before serving out their terms.

Rawlings, a charismatic former air force pilot, seized power in 1979, executing three former heads of state. He restored civilian rule but seized power again in 1981. He ruled unchallenged for 15 years before winning a popular mandate in 1992 elections.
A former socialist firebrand, he embraced Western-style free-market economics, winning plaudits from the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

The main opposition went into the 1992 elections in disarray and boycotted the parliamentary poll. Against the odds, Kufuor's New Patriotic Party and the People's Convention Party (PCP) formed a common front for this year's elections.
The PCP, which did not exist in 1992, follows the socialist line promoted by Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first president.
